The boast was notable given Trump's long history of losing legal cases, failed business litigation, and well-documented legal misjudgments. merged_description_snapshot.description_long: A federal lawsuit filed in the Southern District of New York on August 12, 2026, accused the Trump administration of violating the First Amendment by selling advance access to Truth Social posts. The plaintiffs were the Freedom of the Press Foundation and The Intercept, represented by several legal organizations. Their complaint challenged Truth API, a service announced by Truth Social’s parent company that offered early access to posts by Trump and other officials for as much as $100,000 per month; the report said at least 10 customers had signed up. The plaintiffs argued that the president was monetizing public statements and providing market-moving government information to paying users. The report noted that Trump held a 41% stake in Trump Media & Technology Group through a trust controlled by one of his sons, and that the administration had treated his Truth Social posts as official presidential statements in other contexts. These are allegations in a newly filed case, not a court ruling. The White House had not responded to the request for comment when the report was published.

frozen_original_record.synopsis: Trump's crypto company, World Liberty Financial, has been approved as a national bank by a federal regulator. This move has raised concerns about the potential for corruption and conflicts of interest.
frozen_original_record.title: Trump's Crypto Company Approved as National Bank

merged_description_snapshot.description_long: World Liberty Trust Company, an entity associated with World Liberty Financial, received preliminary conditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in August 2026 to pursue a national trust bank charter. The OCC letter says the application met certain regulatory and policy requirements, but it makes clear that additional conditions must be satisfied before the company can open and conduct the proposed fiduciary business. This is not the same as an unconditional charter or a finding that the firm is already operating as a national bank. The crypto venture was launched by Trump and his sons, making the proposed institution a source of conflict-of-interest concerns because the president and his family have financial interests in the company. Those concerns are political and ethical questions; the approval letter itself does not find misconduct. HuffPost described the development as preliminary approval, and Bloomberg reported that the applicant was World Liberty Trust Co. The accurate event is a regulator’s conditional step in a chartering process. Future operations depend on the company meeting requirements and receiving the remaining permissions, so the title’s shorthand should not imply a completed bank launch.
merged_description_snapshot.description_medium: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted preliminary conditional approval for World Liberty Trust Company, a proposed national trust bank tied to Trump’s crypto venture. The approval is not a final charter or permission to begin full operations; the company must satisfy regulatory conditions. The distinction matters because early headlines described the firm as “approved as a national bank.”
merged_description_snapshot.description_short: Trump's Crypto Company Approved as National Bank
merged_description_snapshot.notes: The OCC letter grants preliminary conditional approval for a proposed national trust bank; it requires further conditions before operations. Bloomberg and HuffPost also describe the approval as preliminary. OCC: https://www.occ.treas.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/interpretations-and-decisions/2026/cd1385.pdf
